paragraphs.en: Is {comprehension} the same whether a person reads a text {onscreen} or on paper? And are listening to and viewing content as effective as reading the written word when covering the same material? The answers to both questions are often “no”.The reasons {relate} to a variety of factors, {including} reduced concentration, an entertainment mindset ( (心态) ), and a tendency to {multitask} while consuming digital content.
paragraphs.cn: 一个人在 <u> 屏幕上 </u> 阅读文本和在纸上阅读文本时， <u> 理解 </u> 程度是一样的吗？涉及相同的材料时，听音频和观看视频是否与阅读书面文字同样有效？这两个问题的答案通常都是否定的。原因与多种因素 <u> 相关 </u> ， <u> 包括 </u> 注意力下降、娱乐心态以及消费数字内容时倾向于 <u> 同时处理好几件事 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: Nowadays, it's common to see an {applicant} for a job reading notes on a screen while waiting in the {department} lobby.However, when reading texts of several hundred words or more, learning is {generally} more successful when it's on paper than onscreen.A large {amount} of research confirms this finding.The benefits of {print} reading particularly shine through when experimenters move from {posing} simple tasks—like {identifying} the main idea in a reading {passage} —to ones that require mental {abstraction} —such as drawing {inferences} from a text.Reading on paper actually holds significant advantages over reading on screen.
paragraphs.cn: 如今，在 <u> 部门 </u> 大堂里， <u> 求职者 </u> 一边等待工作面试，一边阅读屏幕上的笔记，这种情况很常见。然而，在阅读几百字及字数更多的文章时，在纸上阅读 <u> 通常 </u> 比在屏幕上阅读的学习效果更好。大 <u> 量 </u> 研究证实了这一结论。当实验者从 <u> 设置 </u> 简单的任务（如 <u> 找出 </u> 阅读 <u> 文章 </u> 的主旨）转向那些需要进行 <u> 抽象 </u> 思维的任务（如从文本中得出 <u> 推论 </u> ）时， <u> 纸质 </u> 阅读所带来的益处尤为明显。实际上，与屏幕阅读相比，纸质阅读具有显著的优势。

paragraphs.en: Physical books don't require {electricity} or batteries.You can read them anywhere, whether you're on the {subway} , on a {plane} , or sitting on a park bench.There's no need to worry about battery life or finding a {parking} spot near a charging station.
paragraphs.cn: 实体书不需要用 <u> 电 </u> ，也不需要电池。你可以在任何地方阅读，无论是在 <u> 地铁 </u> 里、 <u> 飞机 </u> 上，还是坐在公园的长椅上。你不必担心电池续航问题，也不必担心要在充电站附近寻找 <u> 停车 </u> 位。

paragraphs.en: Reading on paper allows for better focus.Screens often come with pop-up messages, hyperlinks, and other distractions that can {interrupt} the flow of reading.In contrast, printed {paragraphs} help to keep the reader's attention on the material at hand.
paragraphs.cn: 在纸上阅读能让人更专注。屏幕上经常会出现弹窗消息、超链接和其他干扰因素，这些都会 <u> 打断 </u> 阅读的连贯性。相比之下，印刷出来的 <u> 段落 </u> 有助于读者将注意力集中在手头的材料上。

paragraphs.en: The differences between print and digital {reading} results are partly related to paper's physical {properties} .With paper, there is a {literal} {laying} on of hands, along with the {visual} {geography} of {distinct} pages.Reading under a soft {lamp} light is easier on the eyes compared to the {harsh} glare of a screen.People often link their memory of what they've read to where it was on the page.Additionally, the reader can easily add {diagrams} and notes to the margins of paper, enhancing the personal learning process.
paragraphs.cn: 纸质阅读和数字 <u> 阅读 </u> 在效果上的差异，部分原因与纸张的物理 <u> 特性 </u> 有关。阅读纸质书时，有 <u> 实实在在 </u> 用手 <u> 触摸 </u> 书本的感觉，还有 <u> 不同 </u> 页面构成的 <u> 视觉布局 </u> 。与屏幕 <u> 刺眼的 </u> 强光相比，在柔和的 <u> 灯 </u> 光下阅读对眼睛更友好。人们常常会将所读内容的记忆与这些内容在书页上的位置联系起来。此外，读者还可以轻松地在书页的空白处添加 <u> 图表 </u> 和笔记，从而增强个人的学习过程。

paragraphs.en: But equally important is the mental aspect.Reading researchers have {proposed} a theory called the“ {shallowing} hypothesis ( (假说) )”.According to this theory, people approach digital texts with a mindset {suited} to social media, which are often not so serious, and devote less mental effort than when they are reading print.
paragraphs.cn: 但是，心理方面同样重要。阅读研究者 <u> 提出 </u> 了一种理论，名为“ <u> 浅 </u> 层阅读假说”。根据这一理论，人们在阅读数字文本时带着一种 <u> 适合 </u> 于社交媒体的心态，而社交媒体通常并不那么严肃，与阅读纸质文本相比，人们对其投入的脑力也更少。

paragraphs.en: Audio ( (音频) ) and video can feel more {engaging} than text, and so university teachers increasingly turn to these technologies— {say} , assigning an online talk instead of an {article} by the same person.However, psychologists have {demonstrated} that when adults read news stories, they remember more of the content than if they listen to or view identical pieces.
paragraphs.cn: 音频和视频比文字更 <u> 吸引人 </u> ，因此大学教师越来越喜欢采用这些技术—— <u> 比如 </u> ，布置学生观看某人的一场线上演讲，而不是阅读同一个人撰写的一篇 <u> 文章 </u> 。然而，心理学家已经 <u> 证明 </u> ，当成年人阅读新闻报道时，记住的内容要比听或观看相同的内容时更多。

paragraphs.en: Digital texts, audio, and video all have {educational} roles, especially when providing resources not {available} in print.However, for maximizing learning where mental focus and {reflection} are called for, educators shouldn't {assume} all media are the same, even when they contain identical words.
paragraphs.cn: 数字文本、音频和视频都具有 <u> 教育 </u> 作用，尤其是在提供一些纸质形式无法 <u> 获取 </u> 的资源时。然而，为了在需要集中精神、 <u> 审慎思考 </u> 的学习过程中达到最佳效果，教育工作者不应 <u> 认为 </u> 所有媒介都是一样的，即使它们包含的文字内容完全相同。 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
